grades.quote: if other harts or devices continue to write to that reservation set, it is not guaranteed that any hart will exit its LR/SC loop.
grades.reason: Directly explains why an LR/SC loop's store-conditional may keep failing. Other harts or devices may keep writing to the reservation set, SCs may fail spuriously, and only eventual (livelock-free) progress is guaranteed for constrained loops.
Covers failure atomicity and undo logging in database-style transactions. It has nothing to do with a conditional-store failure in a CPU atomic update loop.

grades.quote: The atomicity axiom forbids stores from other harts from being interleaved in global memory order between an LR and the SC paired with that LR.
grades.reason: Gives useful diagnostic detail on when an SC can fail. A store from another hart between the LR and its paired SC breaks the reservation. SC success is permitted but not guaranteed. Cache-line-granularity tracking and false sharing are also discussed. It does not directly diagnose a repeated-failure loop.

grades.quote: sc.w t0, a2, (a0)    # Try to update. bnez t0, cas         # Retry if store-conditional failed.
grades.reason: Shows a typical LR/SC retry loop (compare-and-swap) that retries when the SC fails. This is context for the loop structure only, with no explanation of why the SC keeps failing.
